prize_parts.citation: for the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling through ligand design and mechanistic understanding

statement.case_for: After the first round I move from B009 to B052 as my preferred single-part prize. The reasons are about evidence and not about counting votes. Four colleagues independently arrive at the same two names with the same mechanistic argument: ligand-controlled catalysts, with defined steps of oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination, turned a harsh and narrow reaction into a general one that has been confirmed for three decades. That is a mechanism-first achievement of the kind I value, and the attribution is as clean as B009's. Two groups independently built the general catalytic method. I wrote in round 1 that B009 is mature and overdue, and I still believe that, but the chair's summary shows that no other member ranks it in the top eight, and the objections raised against it by Sparr, Zou and Chabes are ones I cannot answer with new evidence. A prize I cannot defend to five colleagues in scientific terms should not be my public position, so I put B052 first and keep B009 as a live alternative.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection to B052 remains that it reads as a sequel to the 2010 cross-coupling prize and that the conceptual novelty lies in ligand design and mechanism rather than in a new reaction type. I think that objection is answerable, since C-N bond formation was outside the 2010 citation and the general catalytic method is not a substrate-scope extension, but it is a judgement the committee can reasonably weigh differently. Kosugi's tin-amide coupling is a documented precursor, and a citation that leaves him out needs the expert report to confirm it was stoichiometric in tin, narrow in scope and not ligand-controlled. Hartwig also appears on a C-H functionalisation entry, so the same name could be honoured under more than one ballot ID. Finally, I give up B009, which I still regard as the more fundamental result: it explains how charge moves through proteins, whereas B052 is an enabling method.

responses.point: Somfai holds that Kosugi's tin-amide coupling needed toxic stannyl amides and had narrow scope, so the general catalytic method with free amines, a base and new ligand classes came from Buchwald and Hartwig, and a citation worded for the catalytic amination covers this.
responses.response: This answers the procedural concern I raised in round 1. If the general method is the free amine with base and ligand-controlled catalysis, then Kosugi is a precursor and the wording 'general palladium-catalysed' in the citation is what keeps the record accurate. I still ask that the expert report state this explicitly, including the 1994 to 1995 sequence, because Zou and Somfai both rely on recollection for the timeline. On that condition I can support a two-name prize and I no longer hold my earlier reservation.

responses.point: Aqvist argues that the mechanistic picture is what makes B052 a discovery rather than a method, and that the citation should be worded around the general catalytic method so Kosugi's stoichiometric precedent is not misrepresented. He also says attribution in B004 needs resolving before a final ballot.
responses.response: I agree with the wording point and have adopted it in my citation. I also agree about B004: Komor, Gaudelli and Liu are each needed for a fair account, and Target-AID is a parallel line, so three names do not settle it cleanly. That is why I do not put B004 in my configuration even though I list it as a chemically inventive idea. Where we differ slightly is on B037, which I would still defer until the PROTAC and cereblon strands can be separated in the citation.

responses.point: Chabes replied to me that the Prize is for a validated discovery and not for clinical outcomes, that base editing has been replicated in many labs, and that B009 has no support from other members so he would need to see how overdue fundamental work is weighed against an actively used field.
responses.response: I accept the first point: replication across many laboratories is solid, and I should not have leaned on clinical safety data as a reason to rank B004 low. My remaining objection is the attribution, not the maturity. The adenine editor depended on directed evolution of a deaminase, which I agree is new chemistry, but Liu, Komor and Gaudelli are all needed, and Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID line sits beside them. On your second point I concede that B009 has no path to a majority, and that is the main reason I have moved. I would still not call B004 more ready than B052, which has three decades of confirmation.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, proposes B002 with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen, and asks what additional evidence would move me on its timing; he argues that fifteen years of independent confirmation is enough.
responses.response: Fifteen years of replication does support the concept. Evidence that would move me is a quantitative in vivo test, for a defined condensate, showing that the liquid-like state with measured concentration thresholds is functionally necessary and not an overexpression artefact, and an expert report that says how much of the cellular evidence holds up. My second concern is the credit. A citation for the principle that names Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen leaves out the sequence-grammar theory of Pappu and Mittag, which is the physical-chemical part. I see B002 as a serious alternative, and I keep it in my list, but I would not put it ahead of B052 this year.

responses.point: Sparr asks whether I see B009 as a stand-alone prize or as a candidate to keep alive for later years, noting the Marcus, Hopfield and Dutton-Moser attribution problems and that she finds it hard to see a majority.
responses.response: I now regard B009 as a candidate to keep alive and not as this year's prize. I believe it could stand alone, since Gray and Winkler carried both the experiment and the framework, but it would need the expert report to settle priority against Hopfield, Dutton and Moser and to say what is new beyond Marcus theory. Neither can be done from the files, and with a single supporter I will not press it against a better-supported candidate. I will keep it as an alternative so that it is not lost from the record.

responses.point: Zou finds the Gray and Winkler science solid but doubts it, because much of the framework traces to Marcus theory and to Dutton and Moser, who are outside the credited names, and asks how much rests on defined structures of engineered proteins.
responses.response: The structural question has a partial answer: the Gray and Winkler work used ruthenium-modified proteins of known structure, so the distance dependence was tested against defined geometries. The pathway versus averaged-medium debate is not fully closed, though, and I accept that this weakens the case that the work is a new mechanism and not an application of Marcus theory. That is a fair reason for my move to B052, where you and I agree that attribution is the cleaner of the two.

uncertainties: Whether the expert report confirms that Kosugi's tin-amide coupling was non-general and not ligand-controlled, and how the 1994 to 1995 priority should be recorded.
Whether the committee reads B052 as a new advance in ligand design and mechanism or as a sequel to the 2010 prize.
How the committee would credit Dutton, Moser and Hopfield if B009 returns in a later year.
Whether the committee could find a defensible second part, for example B002 or B004, within a three-person limit once Buchwald and Hartwig take two places.
statement.conflict_note: My earlier disclosure stands: B009 is close to my own research field, and I considered that a scientific closeness and not a personal tie. By moving to B052 I no longer rely on a candidate close to my field, and I no longer need to flag my preference as potentially overweighted. I have no personal or institutional connection to Buchwald, Hartwig or Kosugi. Xiaodong Zou is my Stockholm University colleague and Johan Aqvist and I joined the committee together in 2015, but neither is connected to any shortlisted candidate, so no recusal is needed.
